messages:
Marta (People Ops): Quick FAQ thread for handback coverage, short grace windows, and a new "review quiet period" we're trialing this cycle. TL;DR: backup reviewers are encouraged, small auto-grace for uploads, and edits enter a 2-hour quiet period before exports. Read below.

Devon (Eng Manager): What do you mean by 'backup reviewers encouraged'? We patched things ad-hoc before.

Marta (People Ops): New guidance: every manager should nominate 1 backup reviewer per three reports (or 1 per team if smaller). Backups are listed in the roster and can be auto-assigned when primary reviewer marks themselves unavailable. Use: https://rwd.in/backup-reviewer to register.

Keisha (EM): If a backup is auto-assigned, do they need manager sign-off?

Marta (People Ops): No manager sign-off required for auto-assign if backup is same band and region. If backup crosses band or region, the system will auto-pend waiting for manager ack (we'll send a 24h quick-ack slack message).

Carlos (IC): What's the 'small auto-grace' for uploads? We had files rejected last minute before.

Marta (People Ops): There's now a 3-hour automatic grace window for file uploads after handback close for minor naming/format fixes. Files uploaded in that window get a 'grace' flag and are imported automatically if they pass validation. Major edits (changing anchors or adding new evidence) outside the window still require a formal addendum.

Review-Bot: Reminder: handback close scheduled Mon 17:00 PT. Auto-grace applies until Mon 20:00 PT for filename/format fixes only.

Devon (Eng Manager): What's an example of major vs minor edits? Adding a missing PDF = minor? Adding a brand-new evidence doc = major?

Marta (People Ops): Good distinction: minor = re-uploading the same file with corrected filename or small formatting fixes. Major = new artifacts that materially change the packet (new project metrics, added code samples, or anchor rewrites). Major edits after close require using the Holdback/Evidence flow.

Keisha (EM): Tell me more about the 2-hour "review quiet period". Does it block exports?

Marta (People Ops): The quiet period is a short hold we apply to a packet after any edit. It delays automated exports (to calibration/comp) for 2 hours to avoid half-baked uploads getting exported. During the quiet period, the packet shows status "stabilizing" in Console. Edits during stabilizing restart the 2h timer.

Carlos (IC): That seems useful. Will managers be notified when a packet enters stabilizing?

Marta (People Ops): Yes — the packet owner and manager get a slack DM from Review-Bot when stabilizing starts and when it completes. If the packet is still stabilizing when a tranche export runs, it will be skipped and notified to people-ops.

Devon (Eng Manager): Any impact on calibration schedules if many packets are stabilizing?

Marta (People Ops): If >10% of a tranche is stabilizing at export time, we'll hold that tranche and trigger an ops review. We'll run a short 1-hour catch-up tranche the next day to keep timelines tight.

Keisha (EM): How are reviewer loads balanced? Last cycle some reviewers got 2x load.

Marta (People Ops): We added a soft cap: reviewers flagged yellow (overloaded) will not receive auto-assignments above 6 packets. The assigner UI will warn and suggest backups or floating reviewers. People-ops can bump caps in emergencies. Review credits are tracked automatically so people who pick up extra reviews show up in the reviewer-activity dashboard.

Review-Bot: Note: reviewer load warnings will surface when assigning >4 packets (soft) and block auto-assign at >6 (hard).

Carlos (IC): If a reviewer is overloaded and still accepts, how do we flag that for recognition?

Marta (People Ops): When a reviewer explicitly accepts an overload pick-up (there's a checkbox), the system logs it as "voluntary overtime". Managers should cc people-ops on the assignment; we'll add it to quarterly reviewer appreciation.

Devon (Eng Manager): Any audit changes? We sometimes need the who/when for appeal windows.

Marta (People Ops): Audit logs now include edit diffs for the 48h window before handback close (who changed what, old vs new filename). Also added the 'stabilizing' state and auto-grace flag. Logs are exportable from Console > Audit > Handback diffs.

Keisha (EM): Does the quiet period affect holdbacks or emergency extensions?

Marta (People Ops): Emergency Extension overrides stabilizing: if an urgent extension is granted, stabilizing is bypassed and packet status moves to paused/extended as needed. Holdbacks still follow the holdback workflow — stabilizing doesn't prevent a manager from filing a holdback.

Carlos (IC): Training: is there any quick reviewer calibration training this cycle? Some new reviewers pinged me confused about anchors.

Marta (People Ops): Yes, we're running two 30-min "anchor hygiene" sessions next Thu (one APAC, one NA). Sign up in the console: Console > Review Ops > Trainings. We'll cover anonymization, concise impact bullets, and common import errors.

Devon (Eng Manager): One more ops question: If my team wants a 24h pre-export freeze (no edits), can we opt-in?

Marta (People Ops): Yep — teams can opt into a pre-export freeze via the team settings page. If opted in, edits auto-block 24h before tranche export and managers get a weekly reminder. This is opt-in and useful for teams with many external artifacts.

Review-Bot: Reminder: backup-reviewer registration link: https://rwd.in/backup-reviewer — register by Fri 12:00 PT to avoid auto-assign gaps.

Marta (People Ops): Thanks everyone. Summary bullets I9ll paste into the playbook: 1) nominate backups (1 per 3 reports), 2) 3h filename/format auto-grace after close, 3) 2h stabilizing quiet period after edits, 4) reviewer soft/hard caps (4 warning, 6 block), 5) audit diffs for 48h pre-close, 6) trainings next Thu. Ping me for exceptions or a quick walkthrough.

Devon (Eng Manager): Great, will register backups and tell my leads.

Carlos (IC): Thanks Marta!

Keisha (EM): Appreciate the training offer 44d"
